la:verb:proicio.gloss: to throw, thrust, drive, fling or hurl forth, down, away or out; discharge, scatter
senses: to throw, thrust, drive, fling or hurl forth, down, away or out; discharge, scatter
to stretch out, hold out, extend, project
to cast out, expel, exile, banish
to let part of a building jut out, cause to project
to throw away, give up, yield, resign, renounce, reject, disdain; neglect, desert, abandon
to rush into something; degrade oneself
la:verb:proicio.html:
prō-ĭcĭo (projĭcĭo), jēci, jectum, 3, v. a.
jacio
.
Lit.
In gen., to throw forth or before; to fling away, throw down; to throw, thrust, drive, or put out; to stretch out, hold out, extend: projectum odoraris cibum, thrown before or to you, : frusto cibarii panis ei projecto,: cadavera projecta, Müll.: crates,: aquilam intra vallum,: aurum in mediā Libyā,: aliquid in ignem,: geminos cestus in medium,: tela manu,: arma, of one in flight (cf.: abicere arma,), ; ; ; : omnibus projectis fugae consilium capere,: insepultos,; : Diogenes proici se jussit inhumatum,: parvam,to cast out, expose,: artus,to stretch out,: hastam,to hold out, extend,: strato graves artus,: scutum, to hold in front, to oppose, Sisenn. ap. ; ; cf.: projecto prae se clipeo,: proicere se ad pedes alicujus,; : ad genua alicujus se proicere,: se ex navi,: se super exanimem amicum,: se in forum,; cf.: projecturus semet in flumen,; .—
In partic.
To cast out, expel; to exile, banish: tantam pestem evomere et proicere,: in exilium proici,: aliquem ab urbe,: vix duo projecto (mihi) tulistis opem,: Agrippam in insulam,; : a facie tuā,. —
In architecture, to let any part of a building jut out, to cause to project: tectum,: jus immittendi tigna in parietem vicini, proiciendi, protegendi, etc.,.—
Trop.
To throw away, i. e. to give up, yield, resign, renounce, reject, disdain, etc. (cf. depono): nec pro his libertatem, sed pro libertate haec proicias,; : patriam virtutem,: spem salutis,: ampullas et sesquipedalia verba,: pudorem,: senatūs auctoritatem,; cf. : diem,to deprive one's self of the light of day, to blind one's self,.—Esp. of life: animas,: vitam,.—With personal objects: aliquem,to neglect, desert, forsake, abandon,: Deum,.—
With se, to rush into any thing: si qui se in hoc judicium forte projecerint,.—
In partic.
To rush into danger: epistulae tuae monent et rogant, ne me proiciam,: non integrā re, sed certe minus infractā, quam si una projeceris te,; cf.: in miserias projectus sum,.—
To degrade one's self: se in muliebres et inutiles fletus,.—
To obtrude itself: quae libido non se proripiet ac proiciet occultatione propositā,.—
To put off as to time, to defer, delay (post-Aug.): quantum odii fore ab iis qui ultra quinquennium proiciantur,.— Hence, prōjectus, a, um, P. a.
Lit., stretched out, extended, jutting out, projecting: urbs projecta in altum,: projecta saxa,: ova,; and: insula a septentrione in meridiem projecta,: ventre projecto,projecting, prominent,; cf. in comp.: ventre paulo projectiore,.—Hence,
Subst.: prō-jectum, i, n., a jutty, projection, projecture in a building, ; ; .—
Trop.
Prominent, manifest: projecta atque eminens audacia,; (from ): cupiditas,.—
Inclined, addicted to any thing, immoderate in any thing: homo ad audendum projectus,: homines in verba projecti,: in libidinem,

.—Sup.: projectissima ad libidinem gens,.—

Thrown away; hence, abject, mean, base, contemptible, = abjectus, contemptus: non esse projectum consulare imperium,: projecta patientia,: projectā vilior algā,.—Comp.: quid esse vobis aestimem projectius? Prud. στεφ. 10, 153.—
Downcast: vultus projectus et degener,.—Hence, adv.: prō-jectē, carelessly, indifferently (post-class.): .

la:adv:proinde.gloss: so, for this reason, hence, therefore (sums up the previous argumentation)
senses: so, for this reason, hence, therefore (sums up the previous argumentation)
as; in the same manner, accordingly
la:adv:proinde.html:
prŏ-indē (abbrev. proin, like dein for deinde;
usually monosyl.,; ; et saep.; ; ; ; dissyl.,), adv.
Just so, in the same manner, in like manner, equally, just, even; usually with a foll. atque (ac), quasi, or ut, rarely quam: tibi nunc, proinde ac merere, summas habeo gratias,; cf. ; and: Scipiades ... Ossa dedit terrae, proinde ac famul infimus esset,; so, proinde atque (ac) si, Lex Rubr. lin. 17, ap. Haubold, Monum. Leg. p. 146; cf.: quā de re quoniam nihil ad me scribis, proinde habebo ac si scripsisses nihil esse,just as if, the same as if,: proinde aestimans, ac si usus esset,: proinde expiscare quasi non nosses,: proinde quasi nemo siet, Ita, etc.,; ; cf.: proinde quasi nostram ipsam mentem videre possimus,; and: proinde quasi aut plures fortunati sint quam infelices, aut, etc.,: haec curata sint Fac sis, proinde adeo, ut me velle intellegis,: faciam, sit, proinde ut dixi, Tragicomoedia, prol. 63: proinde ut commodumst et lubet,: proinde ut quisque fortunā utitur, ita praecellet,; cf., in the reverse order: quia, ut vos mihi domi eritis proinde ego ero fama foris,; : si proinde amentur mulieres diu quam lavant,: equidem diis habeo gratiam, non proinde quia natus est quam, etc. (Gr. οὐχ οὕτως ... ὡς), .—Absol.: hunc filii loco non proinde habere turpe mihi videtur, Planc. ap. ; : ut, sive dulcis esset sapor uvae sive acidus, proinde aestimarent,; .—
Hence, therefore, accordingly, then, in expressions of advice, exhortation, encouragement, etc.: proinde actutum istuc quid sit quod scire expetis eloquere,: proinde istud facias ipse, quod faciamus nobis suades,: proinde hinc vos amolimini,: proinde aperte dice, quid sit, quod times, Naev. ap. (Trag. Rel. v. 63 Rib.): proin tu fac, apud te ut sies,; : proinde aut exeant aut quiescant,; : proinde parati intentique essent signo dato Romanos invadere,; : proinde tona eloquio, solitum tibi!: proinde ne gravarentur,; ; ; ; ; ; .

senses: a projection; (also) the right to build a projection
la:noun:proiectio.html:
prōjectĭo, ōnis, f.
id.
,
a throwing forward, a stretching out.
Lit.: brachii, i e. extension (opp. contractio), : projectiones aquae, jets, Fest. s. v. tullios, p. 352 Müll.—
Transf., concr., like projectura, a projection, in buildings; also,the right to build a projection,, §§ 5 and 6.
